authenticate.description: Start the encrypted challenge flow. This is inert; complete it with the custom encrypted QUERY envelope, not a plain action command.

hello.description: Unencrypted version probe; SERVER_HELLO must report apiVersion 3.

ping.description: Application keepalive; expect PONG and treat a missing reply as a broken connection.

methods.notes: Use the service instance name as serial identity; do not publish a real serial in examples or logs.

identification.notes: Service instance is the device serial; hostname is remootio_<serial>.local. API must already be enabled by the owner.

device.name: Remootio 2 / 3 garage-door controller (WebSocket API v3)
device.notes:
Official local WebSocket API v3 on ws://<device-ip>:8080 for device software 2.24 and later. An owner with the master key enables the API in the vendor app and receives an API Secret Key and API Auth Key (each 64 hex characters, 32 bytes). mDNS advertises _remootio._tcp with the serial as instance name and hostname remootio_<serial>.local. One API connection is allowed at a time. EasyConnect/Internet access is optional.
Consumer integration is identify_only: this project does not ship the dedicated encrypted WebSocket session handler. The protocol blocks and QUERY-only stdlib vectors preserve implementation facts, not live app telemetry/control; supported status requires that dedicated handler.
BASIC frames such as HELLO, PING and AUTH are JSON text. Sensitive actions, responses and events are NOT plain commands: they are compact JSON plaintext inside an ENCRYPTED envelope using AES-256-CBC with PKCS7, a random 16-byte IV, and HMAC-SHA256 over the exact compact data object (iv first, payload second). The transport is ws://, so envelope authentication and validation are mandatory. Verify MAC before decryption and use constant-time compare.
AUTH starts a new session. The challenge is encrypted with the API Secret Key and authenticated with the API Auth Key; it issues a base64 session key and initialActionId. Later plaintext uses the session key for AES while the same API Auth Key remains the HMAC key. Complete authentication with a read-only QUERY whose id is initialActionId+1. Every later action increments by one modulo 0x7fffffff. A wrong action id or authentication error closes the session; reconnect and authenticate afresh rather than replaying.
BLE also exists for owner setup/control, but its enrolment and complete command framing are not established. The BLE map below is informational and deliberately has no BLE commands. Remootio 1, Remootio Pro, wireless-sensor pairing and OTA are not claimed by this API-v3 profile.

openness.notes: The LAN interface is published for third-party clients. BLE details are reported from separate public app analysis and are not presented as part of the documented LAN API.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: A master-key owner must enable the WebSocket API in the app; this is an administrative gate, not an always-open pairing window.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the other WebSocket API client, then reconnect and complete a new AUTH + QUERY session. No OS Bluetooth bond is involved.

pairing.notes: This block describes the Wi-Fi API's application-layer authorization, not Bluetooth bonding. Each socket starts unauthenticated and must complete the encrypted challenge plus a valid next-id action within 30 seconds.

unpair.notes: Disable the WebSocket API to withdraw LAN access. Whether key rotation is available and how it affects saved clients is unverified.

safety_advisory.detail: The contact sensor reports state; it is not a safety interlock and does not make remote actuation safe. Test on a bench controller where possible. QUERY is the only action encoded by this spec's tests. No actuation is performed by this project, and action definitions are not plain JSON commands that a generic WebSocket renderer may send directly.
safety_advisory.summary: TRIGGER, OPEN and CLOSE can move a real gate or garage door. Keep the opening clear and under direct observation.

issued_to_client: API Secret Key: 64 hex characters decoded to 32 bytes; encrypts only the initial challenge
API Auth Key: 64 hex characters decoded to 32 bytes; HMAC-SHA256 key for every encrypted frame
API Session Key: base64-decoded 32-byte per-connection AES key from CHALLENGE
lastActionId: local per-session replay counter, never reused within that session
credentials.notes: BLE provisioning protection is unresolved, hence unknown rather than a claim of TLS or plaintext. The WebSocket itself is plaintext ws://; sensitive payloads are protected at the application envelope. Never commit keys, QR payloads, serials or owner IP addresses.
stored_on_device: API enabled/logging mode and API authorization material

factory_reset.description: The manual identifies the reset button but the reviewed procedure did not establish a safe sequence. No candidate hold is published. Disabling the API or disconnecting a client is not a factory reset.
factory_reset.effect: A physical reset button is shown in the Remootio 3 manual, but its hold time and exact cleared-state list were not established. Assume owner keys, Wi-Fi credentials and API settings may be affected and do not promise that opener wiring/configuration survives.

methods.description: Use phone-direct BLE owner setup, then explicitly enable local API v3 and record its credentials.
methods.name: Owner app Wi-Fi setup, then enable WebSocket API

steps.action: Power the installed controller, keep the gate opening clear, and enable phone Bluetooth.
In the vendor app choose to set up a new device and complete owner/Wi-Fi setup.
steps.expect: Manual-backed completion indication: the controller blinks once every five seconds after setup and stays continuously illuminated after Wi-Fi setup.

steps.action: As the master-key owner, enable WebSocket API with or without event logging in the device software settings.
steps.expect: The app displays the API Secret Key, API Auth Key and local IP address; mDNS advertises _remootio._tcp on port 8080.

steps.action: Store both keys in a secret store, connect to ws://<device-ip>:8080, send HELLO and require SERVER_HELLO apiVersion 3.
steps.expect: API version 3 and the expected serial; no actuation is needed to verify the socket.

steps.action: Send AUTH, validate/decrypt the challenge, then send an encrypted QUERY with the next action id.
steps.expect: A valid encrypted QUERY response completes authentication and returns state without triggering the relay.

causes: Wrong key encoding, non-compact MAC input, iv/payload order changed, bad padding or reused/wrong action id.
Another API client holds the sole connection; disconnect it and start a new session.
The API is disabled, the controller is not on Wi-Fi, or software is older than 2.24. BLE-only access does not imply the LAN API is enabled.
troubleshooting.symptom: No mDNS service or port 8080 listener appears.

setup.notes: LAN API setup requires an owner/master key in the vendor app and a Wi-Fi joined controller. The app supplies the two API keys and device address. BLE setup itself is manual-backed; its internal enrolment is not.

rejoin.notes: BLE owner setup remains the recovery route when the old Wi-Fi network is unreachable. Re-run the app's Wi-Fi setup for the new network, then confirm whether API v3 remains enabled and re-authenticate a new session. Exact preservation of API keys across re-provisioning is unverified.

steps.action: Keep the master key and both API keys in the owner's secret store before replacing the router.
Use phone-direct BLE vendor setup to join the new Wi-Fi network; do not trigger the control output.
Rediscover _remootio._tcp, verify HELLO apiVersion 3 and complete a fresh AUTH + QUERY session.

testing.notes: No Remootio hardware, radio capture, account, cloud session or actuation was used. API v3 is vendor-documented and independently implemented. Crypto vectors below are newly generated from invented keys and a QUERY action; no credentials or payloads from the official examples are copied.

variants.notes: API v3 on device software 2.24+. Secondary relay behavior is hardware/configuration-specific and excluded.
Current controller with the verified owner manual linked below; API v3 on device software 2.24+.

entities.name: Garage Door
entities.notes: State comes from authenticated QUERY responses and StateChange events through protocol_details.websocket_api_v3: open, closed or unavailable (no sensor). Actuation is deliberately not bound as a generic plain JSON command; a client must implement the encrypted session and show the advanced safety warning before offering OPEN/CLOSE/TRIGGER.

evidence.app_static_analysis: Public app analysis supplied BLE endpoint roles and chunk constants. Full BLE enrolment and command framing remain deliberately unimplemented.
evidence.documentation_review: Official API v3 at d5f3cdd1f51711571065f363081db4295ec76f58 supplied the endpoint, one-client limit, mDNS identity, frame authentication, action counter, QUERY and advanced action/event shapes. Official manual supplied owner setup and LED outcomes.
evidence.open_questions: Owner-controlled redacted BLE commissioning/session capture, Remootio Pro/2/3 API matrix, reset effect, key rotation and API-key preservation across Wi-Fi re-provisioning.
evidence.public_implementation: ivgg-me/aioremootio at 7bf2b4856fe7494d52b2d048e06725504cb366f4 independently corroborates compact data JSON, AES-CBC and HMAC-SHA256. It implements LAN only and is not evidence for the BLE framing.

close.advanced_reason: Commands a physical closing action when state is open; crush/pinch risk requires direct observation.
close.response: No sensor gives ERR_NO_SENSOR. Already closed may succeed with relayTriggered false.

actions.excluded: TRIGGER_SECONDARY, RESTART, duration/latch behavior and all key-management operations are outside this spec.

open.advanced_reason: Commands a physical opening action when state is closed; can move a gate/garage door.
open.response: No sensor gives ERR_NO_SENSOR. Already open may succeed with relayTriggered false. State alone is not a safety check.

response_fields.errorCode: error text when success is false
response_fields.t100ms: unsigned uptime counter; multiply by 0.1 seconds

trigger.advanced_reason: Pulses or holds the physical control output and can move the gate. Optional duration is integer minutes; omitted in this spec's tests and examples.
trigger.response: Check success, state, relayTriggered and errorCode (including ERR_RELAY_BUSY).

error.handling: Surface authentication/input/timeout errors; do not retry an action automatically.

algorithm_steps: Serialize the inner action/response/event as compact JSON with no whitespace and Latin-1-compatible content.
Apply PKCS7 padding to a multiple of 16 bytes; always add 1..16 bytes, including a full block when already aligned.
Generate a fresh random 16-byte IV and encrypt padded plaintext with AES-256-CBC. Use API Secret Key only for CHALLENGE decryption; use session key after the challenge.
Construct EXACTLY the compact JSON string {"iv":"<iv64>","payload":"<payload64>"}, preserving iv then payload order and base64 spelling.
Compute HMAC-SHA256 over those exact bytes using API Auth Key; base64-encode the 32-byte result into mac.
On receive, require object shape and exact base64 lengths, reconstruct data compactly with iv first, verify HMAC in constant time BEFORE AES decryption, then validate PKCS7 and parse JSON.

key_encodings.api_auth_key: 64 hex chars -> 32 bytes; HMAC key for challenge and all subsequent frames
key_encodings.api_secret_key: 64 hex chars -> 32 bytes; AES key for the initial CHALLENGE only
key_encodings.iv: base64 -> exactly 16 bytes; cryptographically random per newly encrypted frame
key_encodings.session_key: base64 -> 32 bytes; AES key after CHALLENGE

encrypted_envelope.openssl_equivalent: openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -K <64-hex-session-key> -iv <32-hex-iv> with PKCS7 enabled (the default). Feed raw compact inner JSON and base64-encode the ciphertext. HMAC-SHA256 is over the data JSON, not the whole ENCRYPTED frame and not the decoded ciphertext.

events.common_fields: cnt (event counter, reset on restart), type, state, t100ms (0.1-second uptime units)
events.handling: Accept only authenticated events; keep event counter separate from action id. Logging-enabled events may identify keys and must be privacy-scrubbed.

steps: Connect and optionally exchange HELLO/SERVER_HELLO. Send AUTH within 30 seconds.
Verify HMAC with API Auth Key, decrypt CHALLENGE with API Secret Key, and validate PKCS7/JSON.
Read challenge.sessionKey as base64 and challenge.initialActionId as the initial lastActionId.
Set next id = (lastActionId + 1) % 0x7fffffff. Encrypt a QUERY using the new session key and API Auth Key for HMAC.
A valid QUERY response authenticates the session. Store lastActionId = sent id. Never replay a timed-out action; authenticate a new session instead.
Validate every response/event MAC, padding, matching response type/id and success flag before publishing state.

synthetic_query_vector.provenance: Newly generated with invented sequential keys and fixed IV; no real credential, device, session or actuation. scripts/test_remootio_garage_door_spec.py reproduces it locally.

remaining_unknowns: Complete BLE enrolment, application commands and on-air MTU/chunk behavior; no BLE command is declared.
Factory-reset hold and exactly which Wi-Fi, owner, sensor and API settings it clears.
Whether API keys survive Wi-Fi rejoin and whether they can be rotated without a full reset.
Remootio Pro and Remootio 1 compatibility, secondary-relay configuration, wireless-sensor pairing and OTA.

characteristics.name: BLE bidirectional encrypted application channel
characteristics.notes: Reported app constants: request 512-byte MTU, 20-byte raw chunks, 16-byte IV/block size, 32-byte keys and 68-byte minimum encrypted message; PNG keepalive no more often than every 15 seconds. These are source-derived app constants, not capture-verified on-air limits. No commands are declared.

services.name: Remootio BLE controller service (informational only)
services.notes: BLE owner setup/control is real but not implemented by the LAN API clients. The complete enrolment, message boundaries and encrypted command schema are unresolved; do not send LAN API frames to this characteristic.

channels.description: Only unencrypted BASIC frames (HELLO, PING, AUTH) belong here. QUERY, TRIGGER, OPEN, CLOSE, responses and events require the custom encrypted envelope in protocol_details.websocket_api_v3 and are intentionally not top-level commands.
channels.name: basic

websocket.notes: Send an application PING every 60-90 seconds and require PONG. Device closes an unauthenticated session after 30 seconds and an idle session after 120 seconds. One API connection at a time.
